paragraphs: Categorized Resource List
Resource by Grouping
Basic Needs & Financial Support
Academic Support & Success
Library & Research Resources
Technology, Software & Online Tools
Health, Counseling & Wellness
Recreation, Outdoors & Fitness
Student Life, Community & Belonging
Identity-Based / Special Population Support
Career, Professional Development & Experiential Learning
Transportation, Safety & Campus Navigation
Arts, Culture & Entertainment
Study Abroad, Leadership & Student Funding
Community / Off-Campus Library & Local Resources

To find out more information about each resource, searching in your web browser for the title of the resource, keywords, or directly asking for relevant contacts in the appropriate department is recommended.
Basic Needs & Financial Support
Clyde’s Cupboard: 100% donation based and free food pantry/ basic needs support regardless of student financial status.
Clyde’s Closet: 7 free professional clothing items per semester (coats, skirts, pants, belts, shoes, purses, briefcases, etc.)
Mountain Lion Meals: up to 3 free meals at eligible on-campus dining halls
Basic Needs Support/ Single Stop: campus screening (survey/consult) for assessing relevant public benefit and support resources
Emergency Financial Assistance: limited emergency funds and loans, grants can range from $100 - $1000
MOSAIC Center: personal care products, sexual health items, community lounge, isolated reflection room, fidget toys, First2Go program, scholarships, events, etc.
Academic Support & Success
Kraemer Family Library (KFL): books, study rooms, university archive reserves, online databases, customized to you research help, interlibrary loan, third floor/top level isolated reflection room.
Excel Science Center Tutoring: free coffee, snacks/donuts, board game check out, and of course science help from physical sciences to chemistry, etc.
Excel Writing & Communication Center: personalized one on one help for writing papers, peer review, outlining and practicing speeches, interview practice (formerly Multiliteracy Center).
Math Center: first floor of KFL near circulation desk, help for Computer Science, math, statistics, physics, Peer-Assisted Study Sessions (PASS) for specific classes, general drop-ins
Academic Advising: Connect with your advisor to answer career, degree path, scheduling, coursework logistics/withdrawals/record questions and check-in with your progress.

TRIO Student Support Services: a federally funded program for undergraduate students to provide additional guidance, resources, academic plans, and Pell grant for first generation students as part of a financial aid package.
Disability Services: recognizes needs and communicates smoothly to professors about accommodations.

Grant Funding: Green Action Fund is a student organization that provides grants to students with sustainable, economic, and social conscious project themes. This includes research, events, projects, and campus features like the bulk refill station or water refill stations.

Machine Shop: The third floor of Osborne hosts the machine shop program for manufacturing, deposition, patterning, characterization, welding, 3D and resin printing, custom orders, carpentry, metallurgy, and more. Resource to provide interested students with a general introduction to machine shop safety, tools, and operations and work on projects.
Garage: third floor of Osborne on-campus student entrepreneurship and business center for meetings and project brainstorming
Library & Research Resources
Library checkouts: board games, DVDs, manga, special collections
Banned Books: semesterly events where books may have been banned at some level in other states, for example, are lent to students as mystery packages.
Library borrowing: power cords (USB-C, apple, etc.), headphones, earbuds, earplugs, whiteboard markers, writing utensils, paper of different sizes, notecards, umbrellas, bike locks, etc.
Textbook course reserves: access to past class material and textbooks for some classes
Study rooms: free reservations yearly with extensive hour availability for individual or multiple person groups
Archives access dedicated section to view public UCCS records, history, and progression
Digital Exhibits: online/events collections for student viewing
KFL A-Z databases: multiple online research, article, and information repository sources
Academic journal access / paywall bypass via UCCS login: many popular journals such as jstor, Oreilly, ProQuest, and more.
BrowZine: collection of peer reviewed articles and research for reference
Prospector: multi-library catalog service
NYT: access with UCCS login
Author talks/tabling: across campus at different location up and coming authors of recent books table, sign books, and chat with students
KFL Card: As a UCCS student/alum/beyond, you have a forever library card at KFL.
Scanning; the scanner machine near the printers on the main library floor is free
Public computers/printing: access to school desktop computers and computer labs is free; printing is free for the first $1.00 worth of material.
UCCS Farm: research in ecology and honeybees has been conducted at the UCCS Farm in the past; it is an underutilized site for hosting biological and environmental science research.
Technology, Software & Online Tools
Zoom: access to this suite
Microsoft 365: unlimited access to products
CU ChatGPT Edu: A learning supportive version of OpenAI’s ChatGPT Edu model for students.
LinkedIn Learning: online training courses and skill building
Coursera: hundreds of full online courses across the CU system for all majors.
Percipio/Skillsoft: provided through the CU system, some free technical certifications
Qualtrics: create survey forms
UCCS Virtual Computer Lab: host a virtual machine on your web browser to access the Adobe Suite and more as a UCCS student
SPSS: sociology statistics application access for graduate students
IT Software Catalog: OIT website lists all applications used at UCCS and for students
El Pomar IT resources: technology support with UCCS owned technology, recycling of eligible devices/donating for class learning
Laptop program: borrow a laptop
UCCS terminal Linux server: connect to the UCCS server with your student account, non-administrator access
GitHub Copilot and GitHub Student Developer Pack: useful for CS majors
JetBrains: Integrated development environment and coding resources
Azure: free through Microsoft student account
Figma Education: planning, cloud-based digital design, UX/UI design web application
Miro: educational templates and class teaching outline preparation
Notion: calendar, schedule, task planning
Student Beans / UNiDAYS: discounted student prices, coupons, deals for students
Special student deals: Amazon Prime Student, Spotify Student, Apple Music Student, Headspace, YouTube Premium student discounts
Health, Counseling & Wellness
Wellness Center: clinic, counseling, nutrition, massage, blood draws, check-ups, psychiatric services, sexual health services

UCCS Farm and Greenhouse: free organic and locally grown herbs, produce, occasionally eggs, a beekeeping program with one-on-one teaching for those interested, mindful animal connection (we have bunnies and rabbits)
First 3 mental-health visits free
TELUS Health Student Support: mobile app for students with 24/7 chat support for mental health
Nutrition Counseling: 3 free nutrition counseling sessions
Health Coaching: free program to help support goals, fill out form to start
EpiPen Autoinjector training and other Environmental Health & Safety Available Training Courses: available through Canvas as modules for a variety of topics. Search this to find the UCCS master list
Free STI Clinic: recurring all-day events (most months) at the wellness center for STI testing and learning about contraception options.
LARC clinics for IUDs: local sexual health clinics offer highly discounted prices for IUD insertion procedures and other birth control/contraceptives
Fitness buddy matching: complete an online form to be matched with a complimentary fitness pal to support each other in health goals and encourage consistency
Wellness Wagon: representatives go various on campus locations and hand out free snacks (example: library)

PEAK Wellness Boxes: fill out a form and receive one of 5 different free boxes available for pick up/dorm delivery with goodies: Safe Night Out Box, Big Cat Cycle Box, Big Cat Naps Box, Wish you Well Box, Big Cat Barriers

Health & Wellness vending machine at UC: first floor of the UC, a digital vending machine with highly discounted useful items with everything from basic medications to cheap contraceptives/pregnancy tests
Vending Machine at Dorms: La Plata for example has batteries, deodorant, contraceptives, dental care products, and more. Located on the first floor of other dormitories too.
Canine Connections: program where over a dozen different service dogs visit different campus locations for pets and cuddles
Mindful movement classes: guided yoga sessions, meditations, sound baths, etc.
Cooking classes: free guided classes with healthy recipes in Rec center Mountain Lion Meet room
Self-defense classes: series for basic hand-to-hand combat positions and situational awareness education
Bystander intervention: QPR and LEAD certifications: webinar/in person activities to learn how to be a better leader and compassionate individual.
BLS/CPR/Wilderness Training: discounted certification courses
Massage chair: remote controlled adjustable massage chair near pool locker rooms and basketball courts
Recreation, Outdoors & Fitness
Gallogly Recreation Center: gym equipment, indoor track on second floor 1/11 of a mile
Alpine Parking Garage Field: on top of the parking garage, open for select hours, is a 1/5-mile perimeter
Pool: free, has water slide, hot tub, at Rec center

Sports/outdoor recreation equipment checkout: free, first come first serve, expansive collection; tents, hammocks, sleeping bags, backpacks, head lamp, bear canister, life jackets, kayaks, bikes, snowboards, boots, portable stove tops and more. Can barrow basket balls, for example, indoor gyms and general sports equipment.
Cheap recreation rentals: can rent bike lock boxes across campus (near Alpine Village dorms)
SOLE Center Climb nights: ladies climb nights and learn to climb free series
First week of school free fitness classes: a variety of 1-hour classes such as yoga, boxing, and cycling. Some themed cycle classes too aligned to different musical artists
Campus Trails system: over 10 miles of nearby trail system
Program Participation Scholarships: recreation center has smaller scholarships to apply for, less well known
Bike/ski workshop: for those familiar with bike and ski repair, the SOLE climbing center provides free access to tools for repair
Pedal Perks: incentivized reward program for those who bike for their commute to campus
Register your (e)bike: with UCCS transportation get a sticker ID for your bike as an extra layer of safety
Field trips/outdoor trips: guided/transit provided experiences at discounted prices such as hikes, outings, overnight trips, and more
Student Life, Community & Belonging
Student Life: study center and lounge
Club Match form: online survey to find relevant clubs
Club tabling: often free give away items
Fraternity/sorority life: communities with their own activities and resources
Religious groups: CRU, Campus Chai Life, Christian Challenge, Mountain Lion Catholic, The Navigators, and more
Political/Social groups: discuss contemporary topics with like-minded peers
Homecoming: mid Fall semester full week of various events
Talent show, Concerts, Costume competitions: various events throughout the school year
Trick-or-treating in the dorms: in front of every dormitory there are candy buckets
Oktoberfest: events with free food/dinners hosted by the Language Center usually or German club for example
SGA Friendsgiving: free food and games
Commuter lunch days: appreciation weeks and designated days with free food/activities for commuter students
DeStress Fest: often before finals, mindful activities, therapy dogs, and more

Back-to-school week events: first week of school is packed with multiple major events, this includes annual the Manitou Springs field trip, stuff-a-stuff, other craft activities, and rotating yearly events
Waffle Wednesday: at the Copper House for International/Study abroad students and programs, free waffles alongside learning about international opportunities
Donut Stress: Excel Science center free donuts on Wednesdays
Clyde’s Birthday: free treats every year on October 4th or October 5th if the fourth is not one a weekday.
Lion's Byte Game Room: lounge for gaming and community hang-out location on first floor of UC
Farmhouse Fridays: past events at the UCCS Farm and Greenhouse where dietitian students cook free elaborate meals for students. Likely to be continued next Fall of 2027.
Climate café: free tea and coffee at monthly event at the UCCS Farm to discuss the state of global warming, pet the bunnies too

Giveaway events: many large-scale events, especially at Berger Hall, have tabled with free knick knacks, and occasionally larger scale drawings for an iPad like the annual Sustainable Speakers Event in April.

4th floor Osborne “animal museum”: Originally established as a wildlife lab, this hidden campus gem houses more than 800 animal specimens, tours (free) must be reserved – ask any biology department professor for more information

Student Research and Survey incentives: student research email lists can alert you of research you are eligible for that often compensates you monetarily or keep an eye out for the annual UCCS Sustainability Culture Assessment with 4 free $50 Patagonia gift cards.
Identity-Based Support
First2Go: resources and scholarships for first generation students
MOSAIC Peer Mentorship Community: Peer mentoring program personalized specialized one on one peer sessions, group studying, and more
Veteran / VA Resources: McCord-Herbst Student Veteran Center for prospective, current, and alum military student affiliates.
ROTC: U.S. Army Reserve Officers’ Training Corps (ROTC) extensive program for leadership training, tuition payment, and more.
IOE: an important resource for campus incident reporting.
HR resources (if student employee relevant): resource to bring attention to workplace issues. Free candy at the HR Office (former Sustainability Demonstration House) next to the farm.

Student dormitories / residential support: the front desk of most dormitories (especially La Plata) has vacuums you can borrow, brooms, and more. They also provide 2 free room lock out supports 24/7 before charging
Career, Professional Development & Experiential Learning
Career Center: T. Rowe Price Center on the first floor of UC has free resume, cover letter, and mock-interview reviews.
Big Interview: website to help practice interviewing with AI interviewers and popular question prompts.
Handshake events: many virtual skill building and informational career pathway video meets
Micro-internships: through Parker Dewey, create an account and locate short internships relevant to your field that are often remote and paid
Forage job simulations: shadow an employee in your workplace of interest virtually
Career Fit Colorado: website with resources and career pathway matching
Career webinars: through UCCS career center
Career course / Canvas pages: most colleges have career specific canvas pages for how to write your resume, CV, cover letters, interviews, elevator pitches and more.
Professional headshots: occasional pop-up events
Undergraduate research funding: summer program for Junior and Senior students with grants up to $4,000
Research travel funding: SGA, Green Action Fund, and other departments on campus can pitch in on/cover travel expenses for those presenting at research conferences.
Entrepreneurship competitions: occasional shark-tank style innovative product or idea pitches
UCCS LEAD Day of Service: semesterly all-day event that is schedule and interest accommodating, free breakfast before a volunteer block
Transportation, Safety & Campus Navigation
Mountain Metro bus passes: every student can sign up for a free bus pass that connects to the broader Colorado Springs.
Campus shuttle: 12-hour service with bus stops across all of campus, departs in about 10-minute intervals
UCCS Safe App: Free app through the UCCS police for campus alerts, updates, safety procedures, direct chat with campus Police and calling 911
Police escorts: Features of the UCCS Safe App to escort students in their vehicle or walk with them. The app also allows you to share your location with a friend and walk and talk
Visitor weekend parking: free across all locations
500-series parking: free parking series, includes the dirt lot near Hybl
Campus maps / accessibility maps: on the school website detailed maps of the campus and entry points are locatable
Lost and found: the UC front desk, Dean offices of various departments, library circulation desks, makeshift lost and founds in certain academic buildings like a third-floor Osborne table

Microwaves on campus: UC Cafeteria, near Big Cat Coffee, Dining Hall microwaves, Crestone Apartment Village at Alpine Valley UCCS Farmhouse, BI Innovation House, the Garage, many offices across campus
Lion One Card: digital ID for students that includes campus currency, access card, and identification in the dormitory mail room.
Arts, Culture & Entertainment
Ent Center events: monthly Theatreworks, visual and performing arts (dance, art, music, vocals, exhibitions), galas, fashion shows
Heller Center: museum on campus for student art and more
Regular-season home athletics: all home games are free entry for students
Pikes Peak Culture Pass: you also qualify for a Pikes Peak Library Card with opens many other access points
Coloring pages: printables from the UCCS Alumni page

Farm books / tea / coffee / events / hang out with the animals: the UCCS Farm has a bookshelf that students can borrow from, you can brew your own tea and coffee, attend farm events or club affiliated events, pet the bunnies and say hi to our chickens and bees
Student Pathways and Leadership
First-time passport grant: provided by the international office
Education abroad scholarships: internal and external opportunities
UCCSlead: program for leadership development, potential scholarships, workshops and leadership improvement activities
Clyde’s Five: special pathway for student engagement and various types of recognition programs
Undergraduate poster printing support: students presenting at mountain lion research day get a free poster sized print of their research presentation
Community / Off-Campus Library & Local Resources
PPLD library card: as mentioned before, students can apply for a Pikes Peak Library Card for additional perks in our local areas
Mango Languages:  a highly rated language app students with a PPLD card have free access to
PPLD Wi-Fi hotspot lending: with your PPLD card you can borrow a Wi-Fi hotspot for up to 3 months
Chromebook lending: also, with your PPLD there are laptop borrowing services

Makerspaces and Recording studios/equipment: In the Pikes Peak Region there are several community locations providing tools, studios, equipment access, and community workshops for creators and entrepreneurs
Additional PPLD digital resources: Libby, Hoopla, Kanopy, Northstar, CustomGuide, databases

Local community resources: Food to Power food pantry, Rad Hostel for cheap overnight stays, El Paso County Citizen Service Center, Community Gardens in the CO Springs Area, Manitou Springs Mineral Springs water tasting, Pikes Peak Library District over 14 branches for community events, parks and trails (use an app such as Strava or Alltrails to find ones near you), Bear Creek Nature Center, Fountain Creek Nature Center and Garden of the Gods Visitor and Nature Center, several free museums to visit in Manitou Springs, annual Farmer’s Markets, and bottom line is to explore what is available.

There are more free experiences than what you may expect if you choose to deliberately seek them out. Colorado Springs is a special area as it attracts businesses, preserves nature and historic sites, and serves a wide variety of communities.
Date
Context
Resource availability Accurate as of October 2026

This project came about as the UCCS website does not have a central location or circulated document that includes every free or discounted resource in an accessible format. It may be particularly useful to Freshman, new students, or those looking to learn about additional offerings.
